```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(omopduckdb)
```

The OMOP CDM does not define everything a protocol needs. An area deprivation index, the rural-urban code of the home ZIP, the
median household income of the census tract, a site's own comorbidity score: none of these is a standard concept, so the OHDSI
tools (FeatureExtraction, PatientLevelPrediction, DeepPatientLevelPrediction) cannot see them.

A **study-design feature** is such a feature. `omopduckdb` ships a small framework, not a data set:

| You write | The package does |
|---|---|
| a `study_feature()` (or a built-in: `ruca_feature()`, `sdi_feature()`, `area_feature()`, `sql_feature()`, `custom_feature()`) | resolves the address in effect at admission once, computes every feature for the index stays, keeps the fitted state |
| a `feature_set()` you extend with `add_feature()` | writes the values as `measurement` rows under site-defined concepts and builds the FeatureExtraction covariate settings |
| the reference table (ACS income, RUCA, SDI) | never bundles it: you supply it, the package only does the join, the transform and the missingness handling |

The same API exists in Python (`omop_etl.study_features`), and the manifest and fitted state are interchangeable between the two.

## A small synthetic CDM

Six patients with a dated address history and one inpatient stay each. Everything below is synthetic.

```{r cdm}
db_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".duckdb")
build_schema(db_path)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = db_path)

zips <- c("19104", "15213", "08101", "17821", "19104", "99999")   # 99999 is in no reference table
for (i in 1:6) {
  DBI::dbExecute(con, sprintf("INSERT INTO person (person_id, gender_concept_id, year_of_birth, race_concept_id, ethnicity_concept_id)
                               VALUES (%d, 8507, 1960, 0, 0)", i))
  DBI::dbExecute(con, sprintf("INSERT INTO visit_occurrence (visit_occurrence_id, person_id, visit_concept_id, visit_start_date,
                               visit_end_date, visit_type_concept_id) VALUES (%d, %d, 9201, DATE '2018-0%d-10', DATE '2018-0%d-14', 0)",
                              i, i, i, i))
}
DBI::dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE person_address_history (person_id BIGINT, location_id BIGINT, zip5 VARCHAR,
                      address_start DATE, address_end DATE, preferred VARCHAR)")
for (i in 1:6) DBI::dbExecute(con, sprintf("INSERT INTO person_address_history VALUES (%d, %d, '%s', DATE '2010-01-01', NULL, 'Y')", i, i, zips[i]))
```

The reference tables are plain data frames (or CSV paths). The column names are matched case-insensitively.

```{r tables}
ruca   <- data.frame(ZIPCODE = c("19104", "15213", "08101", "17821"), RUCA_CODE = c("1", "2.1", "4", "99"))
sdi    <- data.frame(ZCTA5_FIPS = c("19104", "15213", "08101", "17821"), SDI_score = c(95, 40, 10, 70))
income <- data.frame(zcta = c("19104", "15213", "08101", "17821"), median_income = c(31000, 88000, 61000, 54000))
sdi_cuts <- c(20, 45, 65, 85)      # the training cohort's fixed SDI cut points
```

## Build a feature set

A feature set is extended one feature at a time, so a study can start with geography and add features later.

```{r set}
fs <- feature_set() |>
  add_feature(ruca_feature(ruca)) |>
  add_feature(sdi_feature(sdi, cut_points = sdi_cuts))
fs
feature_set_columns(fs)
```

`area_feature()` turns *any* ZIP-keyed number into a feature. Median household income is right-skewed, so use `log1p`; a
`percentile` transform instead puts every site on the training distribution (see the cross-site vignette).

```{r income}
add_feature(fs, area_feature("income", income, "median_income", transform = "log1p"))
feature_set_columns(fs)
```

## Compute for the index stays

`stays_from_cohort()` turns a cohort table into the index stays; here we use every inpatient visit (the default).

```{r compute}
wide <- compute_features(fs, con)
wide[order(wide$stay_id), ]
```

* The address is the one **in effect at admission** (the rule of `derive_geography_features()`), never a later one.
* A ZIP missing from a table gives `NA` and `income_missing = 1` (patient 6); turn the indicator off with
  `missing_indicator = FALSE` or fill with the training median using `impute = TRUE`.
* RUCA 99 ("not coded") lands in small town / rural as in the reference study; pass `code_99_missing = TRUE` to treat it as unknown.

## Make it visible to OHDSI tools

`write_feature_set()` stores each value as a `measurement` row dated the admission date, under a site-defined concept
(>= 2,000,000,000). SDI and RUCA keep the ids of `GEOGRAPHY_CONCEPT_IDS`, so earlier work stays compatible; everything else is
registered for you.

```{r write}
concepts <- write_feature_set(fs, con, wide)
format(vapply(concepts, function(x) as.numeric(x[[1]]), numeric(1)), scientific = FALSE)
cat(feature_set_extraction_r(fs, concepts))
```

`feature_set_covariate_settings(fs, concepts)` returns the same thing as a real FeatureExtraction object:

```{r fe, eval = requireNamespace("FeatureExtraction", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("DatabaseConnector", quietly = TRUE)}
DBI::dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS cohort")
DBI::dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE cohort (cohort_definition_id INT, subject_id BIGINT, cohort_start_date DATE, cohort_end_date DATE)")
DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSERT INTO cohort SELECT 1, person_id, visit_start_date, visit_end_date FROM visit_occurrence")
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

conn <- DatabaseConnector::connect(DatabaseConnector::createConnectionDetails(dbms = "duckdb", server = db_path))
cov <- FeatureExtraction::getDbCovariateData(
  connection = conn, cdmDatabaseSchema = "main", cohortTable = "cohort", cohortDatabaseSchema = "main",
  cohortIds = 1, rowIdField = "subject_id", aggregated = FALSE,
  covariateSettings = feature_set_covariate_settings(fs, concepts))
DatabaseConnector::disconnect(conn)
head(as.data.frame(cov$covariateRef)[, c("covariateId", "covariateName")])
```

From there the covariates feed PatientLevelPrediction exactly like any other FeatureExtraction output. `SQL`-defined or custom-R
features (below) take the same path.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
if (DBI::dbIsValid(con)) DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
unlink(db_path)
```

## Your own feature

Three ways, from least to most code:

```{r own, eval = FALSE}
# 1. A SQL query over the OMOP tables, reading the view `_stays` (person_id, stay_id, admit_date)
prior_ed <- sql_feature("n_prior_ed", "
  SELECT s.stay_id, CAST(count(*) AS DOUBLE) AS n_prior_ed
  FROM _stays s JOIN visit_occurrence v
    ON v.person_id = s.person_id AND v.visit_concept_id = 9203 AND v.visit_start_date < s.admit_date
  GROUP BY 1", columns = "n_prior_ed")

# 2. Your own R function: fn(con, stays) -> stay_id + the numeric columns
frailty <- custom_feature("frailty", "frailty_index", function(con, stays) my_frailty_index(con, stays))

# 3. A complete study_feature() with fitted state, requirements and concept ids (see ?study_feature)
```

The contract is the author's: a feature may only use data dated before the index date (or during the stay when the protocol
says so). Nothing in the framework reads events after discharge.

Next: *Study features across sites* shows how fitted state (SDI cut points, a percentile grid) travels with a model, and how
this feeds the deep-learning datasets.
